purpose: Crizotinib is used to treat a certain type of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) that has spread to other parts of the body. It is specifically for patients whose cancer has a change (mutation) in the ALK or ROS1 gene. Your doctor will do a special test to confirm your cancer has this gene change before prescribing this medicine.
how_it_works: Your cancer grows because of abnormal proteins made by mutated genes like ALK or ROS1. Think of these proteins as faulty 'on switches' that keep telling cancer cells to grow and multiply. Crizotinib works by blocking these faulty switches, which helps slow down or stop the cancer from growing and spreading.
common_side_effects: Vision changes (like seeing flashes or blurry vision, especially when moving from light to dark), nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, constipation, swelling in hands or feet, feeling tired, decreased appetite, and dizziness. You may also notice your liver blood tests become abnormal, which is why regular blood tests are important.
warnings: This medicine can cause serious liver problems — watch for yellowing of skin or eyes, dark urine, or stomach pain and call your doctor right away. It can also cause severe lung problems (pneumonitis) with symptoms like new or worsening shortness of breath or cough. Rarely, it can cause dangerous heart rhythm changes (QT prolongation). Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice. Do not use if you are pregnant or breastfeeding, as it can harm the baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for some time after.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 250 mg taken by mouth twice a day (morning and evening), with or without food. Swallow the capsules whole — do not crush or chew them. Try to take it at the same times each day. If you miss a dose and your next dose is more than 6 hours away, take the missed dose. If it is less than 6 hours until your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule.
